chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh from Abu al-Hasan (the last one), peace be upon him, who said:
I said to him, 'The prayer time arrives while the man is in Al-Bayda' (the open field/outskirts). He said, 'He should move aside from the main path to the right and to the left, and then pray.'

key_terms.الْجَوَادِّ: The main paths or thoroughfares (plural of جَادَّة)
key_terms.بِالْبَيْدَاءِ: In the open field or outskirts (a place without buildings or walls)
key_terms.يَمْنَةً وَ يَسْرَةً: To the right and to the left

ai.seo_question: How should one perform prayer in an open field to avoid disturbing others?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the permissibility of praying in open fields (Al-Bayda) by emphasizing the principle of *ihtiyat* (precaution) against *fitnah* or distraction from passersby. It reflects the Shia juristic focus on maintaining the sanctity and concentration (*khushu*) of prayer even in informal settings, requiring the worshipper to step aside from the main thoroughfare (*al-jawadd*) to ensure privacy. This ruling underscores the balance between the flexibility of prayer locations and the social etiquette of avoiding disturbance to others.
